skill.name: tool-design

skill.summary: Design clear, reliable tool interfaces that AI agents can select, call, and recover from effectively.

content.user_title: Design Reliable Tools for AI Agents
content.value_statement: Ambiguous tools cause incorrect calls, wasted context, and poor recovery from errors. This skill provides practical patterns for clear descriptions, schemas, responses, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Structures tool descriptions around purpose, usage triggers, inputs, returns, and errors.
Guides tool consolidation, separation, namespacing, and collection sizing.
Recommends concise and detailed response formats for context efficiency.
Provides patterns for actionable validation, rate-limit, and missing-data errors.
Supplies Python templates for descriptions, error messages, and tool schemas.
Defines evaluation criteria and agent-based testing workflows.
limitations: The skill provides design guidance and local templates; it does not deploy or invoke tools.
The Python generator references helper functions and evaluator methods that are not implemented.
Recommendations are framework-neutral and may require adaptation to specific tool runtimes.
Suggested tool counts are guidelines, not validated limits for every model or application.

use_cases.title: Define a New Agent Tool
use_cases.description: Create an unambiguous description, parameter contract, response format, and recovery guidance before implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve an MCP Tool Collection
use_cases.description: Review overlapping tools, standardize names, and clarify selection boundaries across MCP servers.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Tool-Calling Failures
use_cases.description: Analyze failed calls and revise descriptions, defaults, outputs, and errors using observed evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Clear Tool Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tool description for [tool purpose]. Define usage triggers, parameters, defaults, return fields, errors, and one successful example.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tool specification: [specification]. Identify ambiguity, missing constraints, weak defaults, unclear outputs, and recovery gaps. Propose a revised description.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify a Tool Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these tools: [tool list]. Map overlapping workflows, recommend consolidation or separation, define namespaces, and explain each selection boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Failure-Driven Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these tool specifications and failed calls: [evidence], classify failure modes, revise contracts, and create representative tests with measurable success criteria.

output_examples.input: Describe a customer lookup tool with concise and detailed responses.
output: Purpose: Retrieve one customer by a validated customer identifier.
Use concise output for confirmation and detailed output for decisions.
Return actionable validation and not-found guidance.

output_examples.output: Recommendation: consolidate sequential availability and booking actions, retain cancellation separately, and use a shared scheduling namespace with consistent identifiers.
State the rejected field, received value, expected format, valid example, correction step, and whether retry is appropriate.

best_practices: State exactly what each tool does, when to use it, what it accepts, and what it returns.
Use consistent names, schemas, defaults, and error structures across related tools.
Test representative requests and revise tool contracts from observed failure patterns.
anti_patterns: Do not publish vague tool names or descriptions that force agents to infer scope.
Do not split one workflow across overlapping tools without clear selection boundaries.
Do not return generic errors that omit correction steps and retry guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill execute tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, examples, and local Python templates.

faq.question: Can it help with MCP tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends fully qualified MCP names, namespaces, and clear selection boundaries.

faq.question: Should related tools always be consolidated?
faq.answer: No. Consolidate sequential workflows, but keep tools separate when their behaviors or usage contexts differ.

faq.question: How does it improve error handling?
faq.answer: It recommends specific error categories, rejected values, expected formats, correction guidance, examples, and retry information.

faq.question: Does the included Python generator run as a complete application?
faq.answer: No. Some helper and evaluator methods are missing, so the script requires implementation work.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace package lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
